name: Euro-area economy
summary: Euro-area Q3 GDP +0.4% and October flash composite PMI 51.9, both above Normal lines; next GDP estimate 13 Nov
state: Eurostat's preliminary flash estimate of 30 Oct put euro-area GDP growth at 0.4% in Q3, with the EU at 0.5% (Eurostat). S&P Global's flash euro-area composite PMI was 51.9 in October, a four-month low, down from 53.1, with French output contracting. Growth has slowed but both measures remain above the Watch lines; Eurostat's next GDP estimate is due on 13 Nov.
for_you: Businesses and workers in the euro area face slower growth and higher energy costs. A weaker economy tends to show first in hiring and in sectors such as manufacturing.
rubric_hit: GDP +0.4% q/q positive and composite PMI 51.9 > 50: Normal line

sources.title: Eurostat — GDP up by 0.4% in the euro area and by 0.5% in the EU
Il Sole 24 Ore — Eurozone GDP grows by 0.4 per cent in the third quarter

why: The euro area is the UK's largest trading partner; stagnation there hits UK exports and European markets.
drivers: Energy prices, German industry, ECB policy, fiscal rules, China demand.

rubric.alert: Technical recession, or PMI < 45, or bond-spread fragmentation forcing ECB action.
rubric.normal: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.
